findings.message: The client-supplied `client_name` is interpolated into a shell command run with `shell=True`. A name such as `x; rm -rf ~` executes arbitrary commands on the server.
findings.suggestion: subprocess.run(["convert", str(UPLOAD_DIR / client_name), "-resize", "128x128", str(UPLOAD_DIR / target)], check=True)

findings.message: `client_name` is never validated, so a value like `../../etc/passwd` reads files outside `UPLOAD_DIR`, and a name containing `/` writes the thumbnail outside it. A name starting with `-` or an ImageMagick coder prefix such as `msl:` can also change what `convert` does. Reject names that are not a plain basename, and confirm the resolved path stays inside `UPLOAD_DIR`.
This adds new behaviour (thumbnail generation) without a test, but the contributing guide requires every behaviour change to come with one.
